notes.meaning: Job begins his answer to Zophar, who was the third friend to speak to him. Each of the three companions has now finished his first speech. Job now addresses all of them together to defend himself.

Job uses sharp sarcasm to answer his companions. He tells them they act as if they are the only people who matter in the whole world. He mocks their pride by saying that when they die, all wisdom on earth will die with them.

Job insists that he has a mind and heart just like they do, and he is not inferior to them. The lessons about God they have been sharing are common knowledge that anyone can see. He has no reason to be intimidated by their proud speeches.

Job laments that his own close friends are laughing at him in his misery. He is an upright man who has called on God in prayer and received answers, yet they treat him with scorn. His suffering shows that even good and godly people can become objects of ridicule.

People who are comfortable and wealthy often look down on anyone who is suffering. In their eyes, a person whose feet are slipping into trouble is like a dying torch thrown into the dirt and trampled on. They treat disaster as something that only happens to people who deserve it.

Job points to real life to show that wicked people often live in peace. Violent robbers and people who openly insult God often enjoy safe homes and have plenty in their hands. This proves that worldly success is not a sign of God's special favor.

Job tells his friends to look at nature to see how God actually rules. Even the wild beasts and the birds in the sky show the basic truth that God made and directs all life. His friends have shared nothing that the animal world does not already demonstrate.

He adds that the ground and the fish of the sea teach the very same lesson. The whole natural world is preserved and ruled by God's mighty power. One does not need special human philosophy to recognize God's hand in creation.

Every creature shows that the hand of the Lord is behind all things. This is the only time in the poetic debates of the book where the special covenant name of the Lord (Yahweh) is spoken. Job shows that he knows the true God far better than his companions do.

The life of every animal and the breath of all human beings are held in God's hand. He gives life, sustains it every moment, and can take it back whenever He chooses. Because all life belongs to Him, He has the absolute right to govern His creation as He pleases.

Just as the tongue tastes food to tell whether it is good, the ear and mind must test the words they hear. Job asks his friends to listen carefully and examine the truth rather than accepting ideas blindly. He claims the right to judge what they have said and prove it wrong.

Old age often brings wisdom because people gain deep insight through long years of experience. Job grants that human elders have understanding, but he uses this thought to point toward an even greater truth. Human wisdom from long life is tiny when compared to the wisdom of the eternal God.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view this verse as an ironic question or a quote of the friends' tradition, arguing that Job is denying that human elders possess true wisdom.

notes.meaning: True wisdom and absolute power belong completely to God. He does not need to learn through time and experience like human beings, because perfect counsel and understanding are His nature. What He wisely plans, His mighty strength accomplishes without fail.

When God tears something down, no human effort can rebuild it. If He imprisons a person in trouble, sickness, or chains, no one can release them without His permission. Men are completely powerless against His sovereign decisions.

God controls the waters of the earth with total authority. When He holds back the rain, rivers and fields dry up in severe drought. When He unleashes the waters, they can flood and overturn whole landscapes, just as happened in the great flood.

Real strength and ultimate wisdom reside in God alone. Both the person who is tricked and the deceiver who tricks them are completely under His sovereign rule. He uses both the weak and the wicked to accomplish His holy purposes, without ever being the author of sin.

God proves His supremacy over the wisest human advisers by ruining their plans. He strips trusted counselors of their dignity and leads them away like plundered captives. He turns the decisions of respected judges into obvious foolishness.

God shatters the authority that kings use to rule and bind their subjects. He strips them of their royal robes and ties a simple belt of slavery around their waists. Even mighty monarchs are subject to His rule and can be brought low in a moment.

God leads even priests away stripped of their official robes and honors. He overthrows rulers and leaders who seemed firmly rooted and impossible to move. No religious rank or political strength can stand against His power.

God silences the speech of trusted, gifted speakers whenever He pleases. He can take away the good sense and sound discernment that normally come with old age. When God decides to bring down a nation, human eloquence and advice cannot save it.

God pours contempt on proud nobles who thought they were untouchable. He disarms mighty warriors by loosening their belts, leaving their flowing clothes untied so they cannot fight. Human strength is nothing when God decides to humble someone.

God uncovers the deepest secrets that people try to hide in the dark. Secret political plots, hidden treasons, and concealed sins are brought straight out into the open by His light. Nothing in creation is hidden from His sight.

The rise and fall of entire nations are completely in God's hands. He allows an empire to grow populous and powerful, and then He can suddenly destroy it or carry its people into exile. History moves forward by His sovereign command.

God takes away the reason and courage of the earth's greatest leaders. When crisis strikes, they panic and lose all direction, wandering aimlessly as if trapped in a trackless desert. Without God's gift of wisdom, human rulers quickly become helpless.

Left without light or guidance, these proud leaders grope blindly in the dark. God causes their plans to fail so completely that they stagger around helplessly like drunkards. Job shows that God alone rules the destiny of all mankind.
